title: 10 · Wardlight: ward observations (tablet)
strengths: Status never relies on colour alone: a shape (circle, triangle, octagon), a word and a number for every state, and the NEWS2 octagon reads from across the station.
Plausible clinical structure: patients sorted by NEWS2, 'Obs due now', 'Overdue 15 min', an escalation banner with a response countdown, a 12-hour NEWS2 strip.
Atkinson Hyperlegible for values where 1/l and 0/O matter; the iPad status bar and the 1180 × 820 layout are right.
slop_signals: Each vital tile says its status four ways: a coloured border, a badge, a coloured end dot and the delta colour, so every tile carries a border and a badge and a chart frame.
Two colour systems fight: traces take categorical hues (green, blue, brown, red, purple) while borders and badges take status hues, so one 'Watch' tile has a brown trace and the next a red one.
Almost every text is bold: patient names, values, badges, tab labels, buttons; little is left to be quiet.
Thirteen patients, six tiles, a banner, a strip and a header in one view: the density of a demo, not a night shift.
fixes: Draw all traces in one ink (or in the tile's status colour) and remove the coloured tile border; let the badge carry status.
Set names and sublines at regular weight; keep bold for the big values and the NEWS2 score.
Show only patients needing action in the left list by default, the rest behind the 'All 13' tab.

references.what: Status tiles above service-health charts in one green; status is a word and a small badge, never a border.
A list with status dots and a summary card at regular weights; bold is kept for counts.
List on the left, one chart panel on the right, one accent colour for the line.
Metric row and a monitoring chart in grey chrome with a single series colour.
